events.title: First Transatlantic Radio Signal Received
events.description: Guglielmo Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal at Signal Hill in St. John's, Newfoundland. The signal, the Morse code letter 'S', was transmitted from Poldhu, Cornwall, England, more than 2,000 miles away.
events.significance: This demonstrated that radio waves could travel beyond the horizon and across oceans, paving the way for global wireless communication, broadcasting, and modern telecommunications.

events.title: Birth of Frank Sinatra
events.description: Francis Albert Sinatra was born in Hoboken, New Jersey. He rose to fame as a vocalist in the big band era and went on to a long career as a singer and actor, winning an Academy Award for From Here to Eternity.
events.significance: Sinatra became one of the best-selling music artists of all time, with more than 150 million records sold, and a defining figure of 20th-century popular music and entertainment.

events.title: Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne Rail Disaster
events.description: A overcrowded military train carrying French soldiers returning from the Italian front derailed in the Maurienne Valley in France after its brakes failed on a steep descent. Hundreds of soldiers were killed.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest rail accident in French history and one of the worst in world history, highlighting the human cost of wartime logistics and safety failures.

events.title: Kenya Gains Independence from Britain
events.description: Kenya became an independent nation after decades of British colonial rule, following the Mau Mau uprising and negotiations. Jomo Kenyatta became prime minister and a year later the first president when Kenya became a republic.
events.significance: Kenya's independence was a key moment in the wave of African decolonization in the 1960s and established one of East Africa's most influential nations.

events.title: Russian Supreme Soviet Ratifies Belovezha Accords
events.description: The Supreme Soviet of the Russian SFSR voted to ratify the Belovezha Accords, which had declared the Soviet Union dissolved and established the Commonwealth of Independent States, and denounced the 1922 treaty creating the USSR.
events.significance: This action was a decisive step in the formal end of the Soviet Union, which ceased to exist at the end of December 1991, ending the Cold War era.
